A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed from O-CRD to ConRAD. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original SWE-Bench Lite evaluations across three LLMs, component ablations, Guardian stability measurements, and inference-cost results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds a mini-SWE-agent experiment, a no-plan ablation, and an analysis of resolved-issue overlaps.

M1.justification: The retrieval, Exemplar Guardian, and backward reasoning distillation procedures remain unchanged. The Thought/Action/Observation integration used for mini-SWE-agent follows the integration already described in v1 Appendix C. Newly supplied prompts and explicit rejection fallback document the method rather than establish a procedural revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use SWE-Bench Lite and historical exemplars from its repositories. The new experiments use subsets of the same repair tasks; changing the execution scaffold does not introduce another dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: V2 adds mini-SWE-agent without ConRAD as the comparator in Table 2 and Exemplar & Patch (no plan) in Table 5. The original Table 1 comparator set and earlier ablation comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds a paired GPT-5 evaluation on 100 randomly sampled issues using mini-SWE-agent, holding its control loop, action space, and step budget unchanged between conditions. It also adds the no-plan control to the GPT-4o ablation. Existing benchmark settings, metrics, and MCTS budgets are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds substantive checks of whether distilled plans help beyond raw exemplar injection and whether benefits transfer to another execution scaffold. Appendix B additionally analyzes resolved-issue overlap with four baselines. These extend the questions tested beyond the retained Guardian, MCTS, and exemplar-similarity analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix H newly states that sampling for the mini-SWE-agent experiment uses a fixed random seed, without supplying its value. The existing three-run Guardian stability analysis and McNemar tests are unchanged; no additional repeated-run or uncertainty estimates accompany the new comparisons.

E6.justification: Original benchmark, difficulty, Guardian, and cost results remain unchanged. V2 adds mini-SWE-agent results of 48/100 without ConRAD versus 58/100 with it, a no-plan Pass@1 of 32.0% versus BRD's retained 41.0%, and 10 uniquely resolved issues relative to four baselines. These supplement the principal results rather than revise them.

T1.justification: The outcome-conditioning expression, reasoning-plan definitions, exemplar tuple, and localization correctness criterion are retained. Neither version introduces theorems or proofs, and the added prompt rubrics are implementation documentation rather than new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about historical repair reuse, inference without fine-tuning, cross-model improvements, and efficiency relative to the controlled forward-search baseline. Renaming the framework and adding supporting experiments do not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new analyses as supporting the necessity of distilled plans, benefits beyond Agentless-specific properties, and complementarity with existing repair systems. The original limitations concerning Python-focused evaluation, sparse repair histories, and unreliable LLM judgments remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 Appendices C–E supply previously absent prompts for exemplar selection, Guardian judgment and reflection, plan construction, and refinement. It also documents rejection fallback and the mini-SWE-agent setup, and adds a public-code access statement in the abstract. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing changes to the original implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds Gao et al. (2023) on in-context demonstrations and Li et al. (2025c) on model-aware in-context learning to support discussion of exemplar suitability. The broader related-work positioning remains unchanged; the APRMCTS/TSAPR reference retains the same arXiv identifier.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the title, abstract, and introduction, standardizes the ConRAD name, and adds disclosure, acknowledgement, impact, and appendix sections. The main section sequence and most method and results prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout, with substantial resizing and relocation of retained displays. V2 adds the mini-SWE-agent table, an overlap diagram, and extensive boxed prompt templates. The existing trajectory illustration is relocated and restyled as Figure 4.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves reproducibility and empirical support. The prompt templates address a major documentation gap in this prompting-based method, while the no-plan control and mini-SWE-agent experiment address previously untested attribution and scaffold-generalization questions. The gains remain bounded: the new experiments use 100-issue subsets, lack additional uncertainty estimates, and leave the unmatched-budget MCTS comparison unresolved. Nevertheless, they materially strengthen the paper while preserving its original evidence.
